factProposals.value: Workers ack a job only after handling it and reclaim work left pending by dead workers (XAUTOCLAIM); delivery is at-least-once, made exactly-once in effect by a Redis idempotency store shared across worker processes.
A job delivered more than 5 times (maxDeliveries) is dead-lettered as max_deliveries_exceeded rather than retried forever.
The chaos drill is runnable code with a written runbook, and only runs against a local Redis.

decisions.statement: Switched workers from ack-on-delivery to ack-after-processing with reclaim.
decisions.rationale: with ack-on-delivery a worker killed mid-job loses that job, which this story's first criterion forbids; the drill demonstrated the loss (2 jobs) before the fix was in.

decisions.statement: Kept dequeueOne (ack on delivery) for DLQ triage reads and existing callers; only the worker loop moved to readNew + ack.
decisions.rationale: smallest change that fixes the loss where it matters, without changing behaviour of triage and earlier stories' tests.

decisions.statement: The drill counts a kill as recovered only when a different worker handled the exact stream message the killed one held, matched by message id.
decisions.rationale: the first version counted 'some other worker finished this job id', which a duplicate copy of the same job could satisfy without any recovery happening.

decisions.statement: The drill was run with each protection removed to show it fails (ack-on-delivery: jobs lost; per-process idempotency: duplicates).
decisions.rationale: a drill that has never failed proves nothing; recorded in the runbook.

limitations.statement: Redis failure is not drilled; one Redis holds the queue, DLQ, retry policy and idempotency keys.
The idempotency claim is the commit point. Real side effects added to workers later must be keyed by the same idempotency key or happen atomically with the claim.
